module.title: Bacterial L-carnitine catabolism through 3-dehydrocarnitine
module.description: An aerobic bacterial pathway that converts L-carnitine to glycine betaine through 3-dehydrocarnitine. An NAD-dependent L-carnitine dehydrogenase forms 3-dehydrocarnitine; a beta-keto acid cleavage enzyme (CdhC/BcoG) transfers the trimethylammonio-acetyl (betainyl) group to acetyl-CoA, releasing acetoacetate and forming betainyl-CoA; and a betainyl-CoA thioesterase releases glycine betaine and free CoA. The thioesterase is either a separate hotdog-fold protein (CdhB) or the C-terminal region of a bifunctional dehydrogenase-thioesterase (CdhAB/BcoE-BcoF). Where carnitine is taken up through an ABC importer, the CaiX substrate-binding protein confers carnitine selectivity on the shared CbcWV choline/betaine/carnitine core. The oxygenolytic CntAB route to trimethylamine, anaerobic Cai reduction to gamma-butyrobetaine, compatible-solute retention, acetoacetate activation, and downstream glycine-betaine demethylation are outside this boundary.

module.notes: Taxonomic scope. The route is experimentally characterized in two classes of Pseudomonadota: Gammaproteobacteria (P. aeruginosa CdhA/CdhC/CdhB with the CaiX-CbcWV importer; P. putida carnitine dehydrogenase) and Alphaproteobacteria (Sinorhizobium meliloti BcoE-BcoF and BcoG). Reviewed UniProt L-carnitine dehydrogenases from Burkholderia, Agrobacterium, Ruegeria, Streptomyces and Bacillales show the dehydrogenase is wider still, but the module context is kept at Pseudomonadota, where the downstream cleavage and thioesterase steps have been shown. KT2440 (Q88R30-Q88R40) remains an orthology exemplar: its LcdH, CdhC and CdhB candidates (Q88R32, Q88R31, Q88R33) are conserved-locus transfers from the characterized P. aeruginosa proteins and have not been assayed directly. In KT2440, Q88R40/Q88R39 form the shared CbcWV core and Q88R30 is the carnitine-selective CaiX component; Q88R38 CbcX is the choline-binding component and is not part of carnitine-specific uptake. Uptake is optional at this boundary: the Cbc/CaiX importer is the characterized Pseudomonas route, and the S. meliloti uptake system was not defined in PMID:30670548, and PMID:19919675 reports that Rhizobiaceae genomes lack CaiX orthologues. Family groundings. PANTHER:PTHR48075 (SF5) also holds 3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA and 3-hydroxyadipyl-CoA dehydrogenases, and PTHR37418:SF2 holds BKACE enzymes with other beta-keto acid substrates, so both family selectors carry a required_function constraint; the family reviews record these subfamilies as functionally heterogeneous. The CbcW and CbcV families (PTHR47737, PTHR43869) are osmolyte-ABC families whose substrate is set by the binding protein, so the carnitine activity is assigned to the complex, not to these families. GO has no exact terms for the CdhC (EC 2.3.1.317, RHEA:47044) or CdhB (EC 3.1.2.33, RHEA:45716) activities; the member gene reviews carry proposed_new_terms, and the module uses the closest parents GO:0016747 and GO:0016289. Those parents are true of the measured reactions rather than ill-fitting, so the member reviews keep them in core_functions.molecular_function with the exact reaction in proposed_new_terms, rather than taking the proposed_molecular_function route that is reserved for activities with no adequate existing parent; when GO creates the two terms, the ids can be swapped in directly.

document.description: bcoE-bcoF (cdhAB, SMc01638) encodes a bifunctional cytoplasmic enzyme of Sinorhizobium meliloti L-carnitine catabolism. The N-terminal region (residues 1-335, 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase family) oxidizes L-carnitine to 3-dehydrocarnitine with NAD(+), and the C-terminal hotdog-fold region (residues 336-496) hydrolyzes betainyl-CoA (N,N,N-trimethylglycyl-CoA) to glycine betaine and CoA, so one polypeptide carries the first and last steps of the route whose middle step is the BcoG cleavage enzyme. In Pseudomonas the two activities are separate proteins (CdhA and CdhB). The purified homodimer was characterized kinetically, and gene disruption abolishes growth on gamma-butyrobetaine, which S. meliloti converts to carnitine before degrading it.

document.description: PA5388 encodes CaiX, the periplasmic L-carnitine-binding protein of the Cbc (choline/betaine/carnitine) ABC importer of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. CaiX has a cleavable signal peptide and an OpuAC-type substrate-binding domain; it binds carnitine with moderate affinity, docks to the shared CbcWV permease-ATPase core, and confers carnitine specificity on it. document.description: cdhA (PA5386) encodes the cytoplasmic NAD(+)-dependent L-carnitine dehydrogenase of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The enzyme oxidizes L-carnitine to 3-dehydrocarnitine, the first committed step of the aerobic route by which P. aeruginosa uses L-carnitine as a sole carbon and nitrogen source; CdhC then cleaves 3-dehydrocarnitine with acetyl-CoA to betainyl-CoA and acetoacetate, and CdhB hydrolyzes betainyl-CoA to glycine betaine. The purified enzyme is specific for L-carnitine and NAD(+), and the gene is part of the carnitine-induced PA5388-PA5384 locus required for growth on carnitine.

document.summary: NAD-dependent dehydrogenases with the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase N-terminal NAD-binding (3HCDH_N) and C-terminal (3HCDH) domains. SF5 mixes bacterial 3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA dehydrogenases (Clostridium Hbd, Bacillus MmgB), the 3-hydroxyadipyl-CoA dehydrogenase PaaH of phenylacetate catabolism, and L-carnitine dehydrogenases (EC 1.1.1.108), some of which (Rhizobiales and Roseobacter CdhAB/BcoE-BcoF) carry a C-terminal betainyl-CoA thioesterase region. SF9 holds mycobacterial FadB2. SF1 holds the animal lambda-crystallins (L-gulonate 3-dehydrogenase), and SF7 includes the Bacillus FadN hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase with an additional hydratase-like domain; other members require separate substrate and architecture assessment.

SF5 itself contains both 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenases and L-carnitine dehydrogenases, so neither the carnitine nor the acyl-CoA substrate transfers from the subfamily label.

term_assessments.scope_reason: This term is not a PAINT node assertion for this family: it reaches members through the InterPro2GO mapping of the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase domains IPR006108/IPR006176/IPR022694. The mapping fits the acyl-CoA dehydrogenases but not the L-carnitine dehydrogenases, whose substrate is a free quaternary-amine hydroxy acid; the cdhA, lcdH and bcoE-bcoF reviews therefore remove the row and record the mapping as a source defect against InterPro. Listed for SF9 (FadB2); within SF5 it applies only to the acyl-CoA members, not to the carnitine clade.

supported_by.supporting_text: InterPro2GO maps IPR006108/IPR006176/IPR022694 (3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase domains) to fatty acid metabolic process. term_assessments.scope_reason: Positive named-member evidence supports Bacillus FadN O32178: curated reaction, NAD/dehydrogenase domains and native yusL palmitate genetics. The additional hydratase domain is not itself a target hydration assay. Neither this member nor the SF7 label establishes the substrate and reaction for every SF7 member, much less the mixed carnitine/gulonate/acyl-CoA family. No new exact-reaction PAINT node is inferred from the broad PTN002455225 oxidoreductase assertion.
